title: Proper surjections give descent of small etale pullback sections
statement:
Let $p:V\to U$ be a proper surjective morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]; surjective means surjective on underlying points. Let $G$ be any abelian sheaf on the small etale site $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Put $Q=V\times_U V$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $r_1,r_2$ and structure morphism $q:Q\to U$. Inverse images on small etale sites and their adjunction units are those of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Then pullback of sections gives an equalizer diagram of abelian groups
$$\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{Et}},G)\longrightarrow\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{Et}},p_s^{-1}G)\mathrel{\substack{\longrightarrow\\[-.6ex]\longrightarrow}}\Gamma(Q_{\mathrm{Et}},q_s^{-1}G).$$
The two arrows are pullback along $r_1$ and $r_2$, using $r_i^{-1}p_s^{-1}G\cong q_s^{-1}G$. Equivalently, a section of $p_s^{-1}G$ on $V$ descends uniquely to $G$ on $U$ if and only if these two pullbacks agree. No torsion, finite generation, noetherianity or invertibility hypothesis is imposed on $G$.

source.place: Tag 0DDW, lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph, proof: the equalizer assertion for an arbitrary small etale sheaf G on U, proved by proper-pushforward stalks (Tag 0A3T, lemma-proper-pushforward-stalk). This node retains only the abelian case of that argument, without any ph-site conclusion.

proof.text: Set $H=p_*p^{-1}G$ and $J=q_*q^{-1}G$ using [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For $i=1,2$, let $\alpha_i:H\to J$ be $p_*$ of the inverse-image unit for $r_i$, followed by $p_*r_{i,*}=q_*$ and $r_i^{-1}p^{-1}G\cong q^{-1}G$. These identifications and units are those of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The unit $\eta:G\to H$ equalizes $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$: both composites are the unit for $q=p r_i$, since the unit of a composite adjunction is the first unit followed by direct image of the second unit. Let $E=\ker(\alpha_1-\alpha_2)$ and $\theta:G\to E$ be the resulting factorization. This is an abelian sheaf: by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact](1) its value on an etale object $T\to U$ is precisely $\{z\in H(T):\alpha_1(z)=\alpha_2(z)\}$.

source.place: Tag 0DDW (lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph), proof, the two direct-image maps and their sheaf equalizer; limits: sites.tex Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf) and sites-modules.tex Tag 03CO(2)

proof.text: Each $r_i:Q\to V$ is a base change of $p$, hence is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Thus $q=p r_1$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. For a geometric point $s:P=\operatorname{Spec}k\to U$ with $k$ algebraically closed, set $W=V\times_U P$, with projections $v:W\to V$ and $a:W\to P$, and $R=Q\times_U P$. The universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $R$ with $W\times_P W$, compatibly with its two maps $\rho_i:R\to W$ and its structure map $b=a\rho_i:R\to P$. No reducedness or connectedness of $W$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0DDW (lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph), proof, geometric fibre of the double fibre product; properness: morphisms.tex Tags 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper) and 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper)

proof.text:
Put $L=s^{-1}G$ on $P_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-geometric-point-exchange] with coefficient ring $\mathbb Z$ to $p$ and the abelian sheaf $p^{-1}G$, and also to $q$ and $q^{-1}G$. The hypotheses are exactly the properness proved above and the two cartesian fibre squares. Taking sections over $P$ and using [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk](2) gives isomorphisms
$$H_s\cong\Gamma(W,a^{-1}L),\qquad J_s\cong\Gamma(R,b^{-1}L),\qquad G_s\cong\Gamma(P,L).$$
Here the inverse-image composition identifications, e.g. $v^{-1}p^{-1}G\cong a^{-1}s^{-1}G$, come from [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The use of $\mathbb Z$ introduces no restriction: every abelian sheaf has its unique integer-module structure, defined by repeated addition; the inverse and direct images preserve this structure. In particular neither exchange application requires torsion.

source.place: Tag 0DDW (lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph), proof, stalk calculation using 0A3T (lemma-proper-pushforward-stalk); Tags 0A3U (lemma-proper-base-change-f-star), 04JN (remark-stalk-pullback), 04JQ (lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point)

proof.text: These isomorphisms identify $\eta_s$ with $a^\sharp:\Gamma(P,L)\to\Gamma(W,a^{-1}L)$, and $(\alpha_i)_s$ with pullback $\rho_i^\sharp$. Indeed a representative of $H_s$ is a section $z$ of $p^{-1}G$ on $V\times_U T$, for a pointed etale neighbourhood $(T,t)$ of $s$. By the representative formula of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], its image in $\Gamma(W,a^{-1}L)$ is pullback along $W\to V\times_U T$ induced by $v$ and $t a$. Applying $\alpha_i$ first pulls $z$ back along $Q\times_U T\to V\times_U T$ induced by $r_i$. Restricting this to $R$ is the same pullback as restricting to $W$ first and then along $\rho_i$, because these two composites to $V\times_U T$ have the same two projections. Equality follows from [def-pc-fibre-product]. For a germ represented by $g\in G(T)$, both constructions pull $g$ back along $W\to T$; [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies the germ of its unit image with the original germ. Thus the identifications compare the specified arrows, as well as their source and target groups.

source.place: Tag 0DDW (lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph), proof: the maps are projection pullbacks; Tag 0A3T canonical map and Tag 03Q1(3) (lemma-stalk-pullback), the colimit description of inverse image

proof.text: The map $a:W\to P$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], since $p$ is surjective. Therefore $W$ is nonempty. It is proper over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence is of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] with the closed subset $Z=W$: closed points are dense, so there is a closed point $w$ (otherwise their closure is empty). By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], the composite $c:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\to W\xrightarrow{a}P$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $e=(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\to W)\circ c^{-1}:P\to W$ satisfies $ae=\mathrm{id}_P$. This is a section on this one geometric fibre, not an etale-local section of the original proper surjection.

source.place: Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson), parts (1),(2); morphisms.tex Tags 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective), 01W4 (lemma-base-change-proper), 01W1 (definition-proper), 01TB (lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points); algebra.tex Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz)

proof.text: We now compute the equalizer on this fibre explicitly. If $z\in\Gamma(W,a^{-1}L)$ satisfies $\rho_1^\sharp z=\rho_2^\sharp z$, pull this equality back along $h=(\mathrm{id}_W,e a):W\to W\times_P W$, which exists by [def-pc-fibre-product] since $ae=\mathrm{id}_P$. The two composites are $\rho_1h=\mathrm{id}_W$ and $\rho_2h=e a$, so functoriality of the units and composition of inverse images [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] gives $z=a^\sharp(e^\sharp z)$. Conversely $a^\sharp t$ equalizes the two pullbacks since $a\rho_1=a\rho_2$. Finally $e^\sharp a^\sharp t=t$, so $a^\sharp$ is injective and the descending section is uniquely $t=e^\sharp z$. This proves that $\Gamma(P,L)$ is the equalizer of the two fibre-section maps. The calculation is valid for arbitrary $L$, including the zero sheaf, and for disconnected or nonreduced $W$.

source.place: Tag 0DDW (lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph), final paragraph: explicit verification of the equalizer on a nonempty geometric fibre using the rational point from the preceding step

proof.text: By [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], taking a geometric stalk commutes with the kernel $E=\ker(\alpha_1-\alpha_2)$. Steps 3, 4 and 6 therefore show that $\theta_s:G_s\to E_s$ is an isomorphism for every geometric point $s$. Hence $\theta$ is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. If $U$ is empty, this same conservativity statement applies to the empty family of geometric points; equivalently all the displayed section groups are zero. No choice of a point on an empty fibre has been made.

source.place: Tag 0DDW (lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph), reduction to geometric stalks; Tags 03PT(3) (lemma-stalk-exact), 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks)

proof.text: Taking sections over the terminal object $U$ preserves this equalizer by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact](1): $E(U)=\{z\in H(U):\alpha_1z=\alpha_2z\}$. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $H(U)=\Gamma(V,p^{-1}G)$ and $J(U)=\Gamma(Q,q^{-1}G)$. Since $\theta$ is an isomorphism and its composite with $E\to H$ is the original unit $\eta$, this is exactly the asserted equalizer of abelian groups with the specified projection pullbacks. Thus agreement on $Q$ is necessary and sufficient for unique descent to $G(U)$.
